**Sooty_Mould:** "Sooty moulds appear as dark, superficial fungal deposits on leaves and stems, growing on honeydew secreted by sap-sucking insects; the leaf remains green beneath the superficial mould layer. On mango, the fungal growth turns the leaf surface black.. Dark sooty deposits on the upper surface of leaves and stems; the leaf remains green beneath the superficial mould layer; does not infect plant tissue but blocks sunlight from reaching leaf chloroplasts; presence of sap-sucking insects (aphids, soft scale, leafhoppers, planthoppers, psyllids, whiteflies) is typically associated."

The description for Sooty_Mould mentions "dark, superficial fungal deposits" and the leaf remaining green beneath, which seems to align well with the test image. Anthracnose mentions "black, irregular spots" which also fits. However, the Anthracnose image `Mango_Leaf_383.jpg` had more distinct, defined black spots compared to the test image's somewhat fuzzy/smudged appearance, which aligns with Sooty_Mould's "sooty deposits".
